title: Dedication: right faith in one Lord; not two sons; Word took ensouled body of Mary Theotokos
english: So I approach and dedicate this discourse to you, most pious empresses. I have composed it concerning the right and blameless faith that is ours toward our Lord Jesus Christ. It especially befits you who are so holy and beloved of God to bind on, together with the highest boasts of the empire, the crown of love toward Christ.

That crown is already fitted to your renowned heads, and the God of all brightens you with unending glories. Yet so that you may shine still more — holding in mind the accurate and unadulterated knowledge of the mystery concerning Christ — I have put together this little treatise, showing through every thought that just as there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, so also there is one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things; and with them, of course, the Holy Spirit.

And having learned to think rightly, we will not put up with those who divide the one Christ and Son and Lord into two sons. For we do not say that the Son begotten before every age from the essence of God the Father is one, and that the one who in the last times came to be from a woman, came to be under the law, is another — but one and the same, both before the true coming-together and union with flesh and still after it.

For the Son from God the Father by nature, taking to himself an ensouled and intelligent body, has been begotten according to the flesh through the holy virgin and Theotokos Mary — not turned into flesh (far from it!), but rather taking it on, and not neglecting to be God.
notes_covered: One Christ; Theotokos; kenosis without change.

title: Philippians kenosis: same one God and human; unchanged Word; economy needs human lowliness
english: For even so he has remained Master of all. These things we have been taught by the saints.

Their words convey wise commands to us: we must hunt what most seems to belong to the holy writings, and scrutinize the truth in the divine doctrines, applying a fine mind to what is said about Christ, tearing down reasonings and every height raised against the knowledge of God, and taking every thought captive to his obedience.

For it is firmly held and confessed by all that the Word from him by nature, existing in the form and equality of God the Father, “did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of humans; and being found in fashion as a human he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross.”

So the mind that aims to discern well the force of what is written about him must somehow be filled with God-loving skill — so that the same one may be recognized as God and human together, and may have his being God without falsification. For the Word’s nature is unchangeable, and he does not refuse the measure of the emptying: the one who economically endured voluntary emptying for us does not blush at his own designs.

He must therefore be seen as distinguished in the dignities of the deity, and yet not wholly freed from our smallness because of the human — for the economy demands this. For if the Word, being God, has become flesh — that is, human…
notes_covered: One Christ; Theotokos; kenosis without change.

title: Joel flesh; human sayings do not disturb; Christ Jesus means Word incarnate; 1 Cor headship
english: …according to “I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh.” Let no one be disturbed even if God-breathed Scripture says something about him that befits a human; rather survey his above-world glory, from power and superiority that is God-befitting and highest.

What is most likely to weaken the mind of the simpler, I will try — as far as possible and as well as can be — to make clear, setting beside each saying the solution that suffices for explanation, God again directing our path into this. For he gives “a word to those who proclaim with much power,” as the inspired singer says.

In the discourse we made toward the holy virgins I set out at great length the readier sayings that have nothing hard to grasp; in the present work I have recalled the less clear. For your God-loving majesty needed to know both — these and those — so that through both what is sound for knowledge might settle, like a light, in your most pure minds. My aim in interpreting each is to be brief as I can; and the discourse on the emptying has been set first of all.
Know this nonetheless: whenever Christ Jesus is named to us, it befits us to understand the Word from God the Father as having become human and been enfleshed.

“For I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God. The first human is of the earth, dusty” — that is, Adam — “the second is from heaven” — clearly Christ. But “just as we wore the image of the dusty,
notes_covered: One Christ; Theotokos; kenosis without change.

title: Christ second Adam our head; Father head of the Word; he became poor being rich
english: let us also wear the image of the heavenly,” as it is written. So the first head of our race — that is, beginning — was the one of earth and dust. But since Christ has been named second Adam, he has been set as head — that is, beginning — of those being remolded through him toward him into incorruption by sanctification in the Spirit.

So he is our beginning — that is, our head — insofar as he has appeared as human; yet as God by nature he himself has as head the Father in the heavens, for the Word, being God, has been begotten from him by nature. That “head” signifies “beginning” confirms, for minds that doubt, that the man became head of the woman: for she was taken from him.
So there is one Christ and Son and Lord, who as God by nature has the Father in the heavens as head, and who has become head for us because of kinship according to the flesh.

“For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, for our sake he became poor, so that you by his poverty might become rich.” See clearly here both the superiority of the divine and unmixed nature and the lowliness of the measures of humanity — and besides these the agreement of both into unity, the Only-begotten having lowered himself into this.

For no word could interpret the riches of the deity, while humanity is exceedingly poor, or rather all that it has is God-given and from above — and before all, even being itself: for it was called by God into existence, not existing before. But the rich…
notes_covered: One Christ; Theotokos; kenosis without change.

title: Rich Word became poor; bought us from the curse; one flesh’s death enough
english: Rich as God, he willingly became poor and became as we are, so that human nature, having come in Christ into the heights of divine superiority, might put away the shame of poverty. For God the Father raised us together in Christ and seated us together in the heavenly places, as it is written. But we would not have come into these things if the One who is rich as God had not clothed himself with the nature that is poor. A human who is poor by his own nature would not “become poor”; that befits more fittingly the One who is truly rich — that is, the Word from God the Father — when he became as we are. So there is one Christ and Son.

“Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, for it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.” While the letter of the law declares cursed the one in transgression and sins, the One who did not know sin — that is, Christ — was brought under the curse, enduring an unjust sentence and suffering what befits those under a curse, so that the One worth all, dying for all, might loose the charges of everyone’s disobedience and buy what is under heaven with his own blood.

He would not have become worth all, if he were a mere human. But if he is understood as God become human and suffering in his own flesh, the whole creation is little beside him, and the death of one flesh suffices for the redemption of what is under heaven — for it was the Word sprung from God the Father’s own.
notes_covered: One Christ: rich Word, priest and victim.

title: Made a little lower than angels; Jesus crowned through death; worshiped still
english: “But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.”

Having made [the body] his own, he suffered in it willingly, and through the passion he is crowned with the highest glories, as having abolished death through it and rendered corruption idle — since he himself is incorruption and life. So when Scripture names him Jesus and says he was made lower than the angels, we no longer understand a human piecemeal and separately, but the Only-begotten himself economically yielding preeminence to the holy angels, because in truth he who is lesser than their superiority has become human. The angels’ superiority is that they are outside flesh and stronger than dying — and the Son has come into these things through the voluntary emptying.

Yet the One made a little lower than angels, because of the measure of humanity, being in the superiority of deity, is worshiped by them, and is seated on thrones that they stand around forever glorifying, naming him Lord of their powers.
notes_covered: One Christ: rich Word, priest and victim.

title: Shared blood and flesh; one Lord Jesus; death abolished in Christ
english: “Since therefore the children have shared in blood and flesh, he himself likewise shared in the same, so that through death he might abolish the one who has the power of death — that is, the devil — and free those who through fear of death were subject to slavery all their life.”

By “children” here he clearly means us who are on the earth, according to what is sung in the Psalms as in God’s person: “I said: You are gods, and all of you sons of the Most High.” As far as what seems good to God and the gentleness in him by nature, we would all be children… but as David says we die as humans and fall as one of the rulers, dragging down our own mind by the passions of the flesh.

How, then, have we shared in blood and flesh? The human soul, having a nature other than flesh, by composition with it in union has completed the one rational living being — the human. So also the Word of God, ineffably uniting himself to ensouled flesh — not soulless, as some say — shared blood and flesh like us, through birth from a woman. So there is one Lord Jesus Christ: the Word of God united the human to himself and even so remained what he was.

And if he himself has abolished death’s power as Life and God, what suffered death must be thought his own, so that as he himself rose he may be said to abolish corruption… “For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.” And since trampling death is beyond the measures of humanity as we understand it, we say that by union — that is, communion with flesh and blood — the Word of God became human as we are, and even so remained stronger than death: for God was in flesh.
notes_covered: One Christ: rich Word, priest and victim.

title: Took Abraham’s seed; merciful high priest; one Lord both offerer and offering
english: “For it is not angels he takes hold of, but he takes hold of the seed of Abraham. Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things toward God, to make propitiation for the people’s sins. For in that he himself has suffered when tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.”

We say the Word of God takes hold of Abraham’s seed: for he sprang from Judah according to the flesh, and was made like his brothers in every respect — at least in consenting to take the form of a slave and to come to be in the likeness of humans, as blessed Paul says. So he has been called Son of Man, and has become brother to those of Abraham’s seed… “so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest.” Merciful, because the letter of the law condemns sinners… yet Christ justifies by faith… Faithful, because he is lasting, continuous, and worthy of trust for what was promised.

“In that he himself has suffered when tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.” For he endured under temptation and endured the cross. Yet the Son has offered himself as a spotless victim to God the Father, so that through his own flesh he might help those who labor… “For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are being sanctified.” So he himself has become high priest according to the human, though divinely he receives the sacrifices from all; himself the victim according to the flesh; himself the one who propitiates for our sins, according to the authority of the deity. So there is one Lord Jesus Christ.
notes_covered: One Christ: rich Word, priest and victim.

title: Salvation from the Jews via Abraham’s seed; Word sent humanly
english: …according to the Word’s nature alone. For how is salvation from the Jews? No one would say that he is from the Jews insofar as he is understood and exists as Word, but insofar as he has become brother to those in flesh and blood by taking hold of Abraham’s seed. So there is one Christ, even if he is said to be worshiped because of the human, though he is worshiped by all creation as God.

“A little while I am with you, and I go to the one who sent me.” Where is the Word of God not present, if he fills all things by the nature of the deity? How then is he sent by the Father? And how does he go to him? So he is sent in a human way, according to the manner and account of the sending, that he may proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind; yet he goes to the Father and God no longer in the same way, but as embodied, having gone up into heaven, that he may appear for us before the face of the Father, as it is written. And if “being sent” is also taken of the Word himself, let no one be harsh: for inspired Scripture is sometimes accustomed to use such voices too; and it does not drag the divine and supermundane nature under places and limits — for it knows that nature is bodiless and beyond boundaries and far from being thought of as in a place — but rather tries to make clear, by human voices, the things beyond our mind. Since the Savior himself also said he would send the Paraclete to us, though the Holy Spirit fills all things: “for the Spirit of the Lord,” it says, “has filled the inhabited world.”
notes_covered: One Christ; Word fills all; sent humanly.

title: Lift up the Son of Man; crucified humanly, lives as God; one Christ
english: “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am.” Explaining to us the causes of the Jewish madness they practiced against Christ, the divine John says: “For this reason the Jews were persecuting Jesus, because he was not only breaking the Sabbath, but was also calling God his own Father, making himself equal to God.” And he has somewhere brought them in saying impiously: “We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a human, make yourself God.” So they have made faith in him unacceptable, thinking him a bare human as such, and not knowing that the Word, being God, took hold of Abraham’s seed and shared blood and flesh likewise with us, yet did not depart from being God — for he is unchangeable by nature and forever himself.

“When therefore,” he says, “you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am.” For he was crucified in a human way, but came back to life in a divine way; and through the resurrection it is believed that he is both God and truly Son of God. And if he is believed by us not as having raised another, but rather as himself raised, then somehow every necessity of the economy requires that the body that suffered death be understood as his own, so that he himself may also be said to rise, though by nature immortal as God. For by announcing the death of one Christ and Son and confessing the resurrection we are justified through faith. So the same one, existing as one and only Christ Jesus, is said to die in a human way according to the flesh, and to have been raised in a divine way as Life.
notes_covered: One Christ: dies humanly, rises as Life.

title: Works of the Father; not two Christs; the child grew in wisdom
english: The Jews once came to Christ saying: “If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.” Jesus answered them: “I told you, and you do not believe; the works that I do in my Father’s name, these testify about me.” What then do those who foolishly divide a duality of sons and split the one Lord Jesus Christ into two Christs say even about this? About whom were the Jews saying: “If you are the Christ, tell us plainly”? And who is the one saying: “The works that I do in my Father’s name, these testify about me”? Whose own Father do we say God is? Of the one from a woman, thought of separately and particularly — or of the Only-begotten? Yet being able to accomplish the works of the deity would not fit a human nature — how could it? Far from it. But since Christ was fulfilling the works of the Father, he would not be understood as a bare human, but rather as God who has remained what he was in blood and flesh. For holding thus, he will work equally with his own Begetter, and none of those accustomed to think well would mock the account of the mystery.

“And the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him,” and again: “Jesus advanced in stature and wisdom and grace with God and humans.” Saying that our Lord Jesus the Christ is one, and assigning to him both the human things and the God-befitting ones, we firmly affirm that receiving bodily growth, and also becoming strong as the body’s parts…
notes_covered: Works of Father prove deity in flesh.
translator_notes: Section continues into §12 on kenosis measures.

title: Growth and wisdom as kenosis measures; Word remains God
english: …maturing little by little; and even seeming to be filled with wisdom is because the manifestation of the wisdom that was in him rises, as it were, in a way most fitting to the advance of the body’s age. And these things, as I said, would fit the economy with flesh and the measures of the lowering; but what fits the nature of the Word again is always to be perfect and to be wisdom. So what is somehow lowered as in emptying is his in a human way, and likewise the God-befitting things are his in a divine way. For the manner and account of the economy with flesh knows him to be both according to us and above us: excelling the measure of creation as God, and somehow all but lesser than himself insofar as he has appeared as human. For where was the humility he willingly endured, if he refused the human things? Yet the nature of the Word is not thought to be in those things; rather he appropriates them with his own flesh, just as also hunger and thirst and being said to grow weary from the journey.

So when you hear “The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom,” receive the mystery as an account of the economy with flesh. That he was God in flesh the blessed evangelist himself will confirm, saying that “the grace of God was upon him.” For he is not said to have God’s grace as one who has grace from another god, but because the child had the grace that would befit God. For the Word both was and is God even when he has appeared in flesh, that is, as a human according to us. And if he is said to have grace, or to advance…
notes_covered: Kenosis measures vs Word as perfect wisdom
Grace befitting God, not from another god.
